eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service and NOAA model guidance for San Francisco on May 30 point to an afternoon high near 64–65 °F, with the 66 °F threshold remaining the leading market outcome at 39 % implied probability because modest warming is still possible under partly cloudy skies and strong westerly winds. Updated model runs and real-time surface observations through the afternoon will determine final resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current short-term forecast models point to a mild start for June in Wellington, with daytime highs likely in the mid-teens Celsius driven by northerly winds advecting warmer air from subtropical regions ahead of an approaching front. NIWA’s seasonal outlook indicates near-average temperatures overall for the region, consistent with historical June maxima around 13–14°C at Wellington Airport, yet daily variability from transient weather systems can easily shift the peak by 2–3°C. Key differentiators among 14–18°C outcomes include exact timing of any frontal passage, cloud cover reducing solar heating, and local wind strength, all of which remain sensitive to the latest model runs as the date approaches. Trader consensus reflects this narrow but genuine uncertainty in the final observed maximum.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: The market-implied odds clustered tightly around 31–33°C reflect the typical early-June transition to the southwest monsoon across Metro Manila, where increasing cloud cover, scattered showers, and higher humidity moderate daytime maxima near the long-term average high of 32°C. Official climatological baselines and model consensus place peak temperatures in this narrow band, with minor differences arising from variable rainfall timing, wind patterns, and urban heat effects that can shift the daily high by 1–2°C. Forecasters note the inherent uncertainty in short-range guidance this close to the date, as monsoon onset can either suppress or allow brief clear periods that push readings toward the upper or lower end of the range.
